header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Meeting type: POC weekly sync (quantization precision sweep)
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Mehta (Brightline Lead DS), Mark Chen (Brightline ML Eng), Elena Ruiz (Brightline Security)
Shared: https://redwood.ai/s/poc-precision-sweep-deck , cost-delta spreadsheet (link in chat)
summary: Auto-summary: 1) Reviewed last week's INT8 and FP8 sweep results: latency gains confirmed (~1.9-2.4x token/sec) with variable quality regressions on safety/QA prompts. 2) Identified three prompt families with >3% drop in answer accuracy under INT8 for the medical QA set. 3) Agreed to run larger 50k eval with KV-cache off/on and mixed-precision fallsbacks. 4) Security asked for KMS/keystore detail; Redwood to share Private deployment checklist. 5) Next: Sam to run larger sweep, Priya to share canonical prompt set, Alex to send cost delta and updated POC plan.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're data five over here, try not to steal too much of your Thursday. I'm Alex, AE on this POC. Sam from eng will go through the numbers.
[00:12] Priya: Hi, thanks. Just a quick note, Mark's on for infra items, and Elena might drop in with a couple security Qs later.
[00:22] Sam: Cool, I'll pull up the slide deck - shared in chat - and then walk through the precision sweep. Quick reminder: these runs compare FP16 baseline, INT8 static quant, and FP8 hybrid on your model checkpoint v3.
[00:35] Mark: small note - the test nodes we used are A100 equivalent in the cloud, same as you recommended. Also we mirrored your env but we saw one warning about cudnn at startup.
[00:48] Sam: yeah that warning is benign, it's the kernel selection mismatch, doesn't impact perf numbers. Okay slide 3: latency and throughput deltas. We saw token/sec improvements roughly 1.9x for INT8 and 2.3-2.4x for FP8 depending on sequence length.
[01:10] Priya: that's great for cost, but i want to focus on QA: what metrics are we using for "quality" here? exact-match, F1?
[01:18] Sam: good call. For Brightline we used exact-match on the clinical Q/A set, plus a question-level hallucination flag (manual), and a small BLEU-ish nlg score for free-form. I know BLEU is rough but gives a signal.
[01:32] Priya: got it. And were these runs with KV cache enabled? we have a lot of repeated context in convo history so KV cache matters.
[01:40] Sam: Most runs had KV cache enabled. We did a small ablation with KV off, results in the appendix. Interestingly, INT8 shows slightly worse regen if KV cache is enabled in long-context cases - likely due to cache quant noise.
[01:56] Priya: hmm, cache quant noise - pf. could that be a mismatch in the cache format?
[02:03] Sam: possibly. We're seeing reduced precision in the key/value matrices after quant pack, some rounding error that compounds for very long histories. We'll run a KV-precision masked run.
[02:13] Elena: quick security question - for the private option, does Redwood use customer KMS or your managed key store? We need to know encryption at rest for model artifacts.
[02:22] Alex: for Private we support customer KMS integration (HSM / Cloud KMS). I'll drop the Private checklist but quick answer: you can bring keys and we do not persist plaintext.
[02:33] Elena: great, please include rotation policy in that doc.
[02:36] Alex: will do.
[02:38] Sam: back to quality: slide 7 shows the four prompt families where INT8 underperforms by more than 3% exact-match: dosing instructions, temporal reasoning, multi-hop diagnosis, and short-clipped completion style.
[02:56] Priya: can you give one concrete example from dosing? I need to see whether it's a safety regression or just wording.
[03:03] Sam: yeah, example slide 8: baseline FP16 answer: "Administer 5 mg once daily"; INT8 returned "Administer 5 mg twice daily" in 2/50 seeds - that's safety sensitive, so flagged.
[03:18] Priya: ok that's a blocker for us if not mitigated.
[03:21] Alex: understoood - we flagged that prompt family as high-priority. Options: fallbacks to FP16 for safety prompt families, or use mixed precision with per-token selector, or keep prefix caching in FP16 for keys.
[03:35] Mark: what's the perf hit if we route those prompts to FP16 only?
[03:40] Sam: depends on traffic split. If 10% of calls are safety prompts, cost goes up by roughly 8-9% vs full INT8. We modelled it in the cost sheet we shared.
[03:50] Priya: can the selector be local, or must it go to the service? we have latency constraints for in-product microflows.
[03:58] Sam: selector can be client-side heuristics: if prompt matches a safety regex, call the FP16 endpoint. That keeps latency similar to single hop routing. There's also model-level flagging in the runtime if you want automated fallback.
[04:12] Priya: got it. Can we see automated fallback logs when it triggers? we need observability for audits.
[04:18] Alex: yes, Redwood Console logs fallbacks and you get token-level trace, we'll enable that in the POC trial.
[04:25] Priya: thanks.
[04:27] (00:04:27) [crosstalk] Mark: question on FP8 — earlier runs were noisy across seeds?
[04:33] Sam: FP8 showed more variance than INT8 in some cases, yes. For deterministic prompts FP8 sometimes matched FP16, other times dropped a point. So it's higher throughput but slightly less predictable across seeds.
[04:47] Priya: how reproducible are these seed differences in an online service? we need consistent answers in prod.
[04:53] Sam: online runs are less about seed and more about micro-batching and kernel ordering. We saw that small changes in batch size change the FP8 outputs for some micro-layers. We're working on kernel scheduling fixes.
[05:06] Alex: to be clear, recommended path for now: 1) run eval at increased sample size to quantify prevalence; 2) pick per-prompt fallback policy for safety families; 3) consider FP8 for high-throughput non-critical routes.
[05:20] Priya: okay. Regarding eval size, last week was 5k; what's the plan?
[05:24] Sam: propose 50k combined sample across your production prompt distribution; we'll run FP16/INT8/FP8 with KV on/off and with caching prefix held in FP16. That's the 50k job in next steps.
[05:38] Priya: is that feasible in-house or do you run it?
[05:41] Sam: Redwood can run it on our infra, or we can give you a runner to run in your env. For security, you might prefer to run locally — either works.
[05:50] Mark: we'll likely provision nodes and let Redwood orchestrate. I'll share access.
[05:54] Priya: good. Any notes on hallucination metrics? we saw an uptick for long-form completions under INT8.
[05:59] Sam: yes that was in slide 11. Hallucination rate up ~1.7% on the medical extraction set for INT8, FP8 was similar but with higher variance. For short QA it's smaller.
[06:11] Priya: what's the confidence calibration like? are logits shifted?
[06:15] Sam: INT8 tends to compress logits slightly, so calibration shifts; we saw lower softmax margin on ambiguous tokens. We can apply a temperature or recalibration layer post-hoc but that only partially fixes generation decisions.
[06:29] Elena: on compliance — will these calibration modifications change audit trails? we need deterministic logs per decision.
[06:34] Alex: logs include model variant, quantization level, and token traces. Any post-hoc recalibration is recorded as a separate step in the trace.
[06:42] Priya: good. For the 50k run, can you output per-prompt variant indicators so we can slice by prompt family?
[06:48] Sam: yes we'll output a CSV with prompt_id, variant, exact-match, hallucination flag, latency, tokens_generated.
[06:55] Priya: excellent.
[06:57] (00:06:57) Sam: now quick perf notes: token latency median reduced by 40-55% for INT8 dependent on sequence; FP8 is slightly better median but worse p95 in some configs.
[07:11] Mark: what's the memory profile? will INT8 let us fit more models per GPU?
[07:16] Sam: yes INT8 reduces activation memory; you can host larger batch sizes or more concurrent sessions. For your 6B-ish model we increased effective concurrency by ~2x on same GPU.
[07:29] Priya: surprising that FP8 p95 is worse — is that due to fallback kernels?
[07:34] Sam: sometimes kernel fallback causes path variance under load; we have a mitigation branch but need to test it in mixed workloads.
[07:44] Priya: okay, timeline wise, if the 50k sweep shows <1% safety regressions on INT8, would we be comfortable moving to a staged rollout?
[07:52] Alex: likely yes, staged canary -> 10% -> 50% with automatic rollback on quality alerts. Redwood console supports that.
[07:59] Priya: what's the SLA impact?
[08:02] Alex: none for hosted, but for Dedicated we can guarantee maintained latency SLOs per your tier.
[08:08] Elena: also need SOC2 control mapping for the canary triggers; please include mapping in the security pack.
[08:15] Alex: will add that.
[08:17] (00:08:17) Mark: quick question about model versioning: when we roll, can we pin older checkpoints for a prompt family?
[08:24] Sam: yes, rollout policies support per-route pinning and automatic fallback to pinned variant.
[08:28] Priya: cool.
[08:30] (00:08:30) Sam: next I want to go through the anomaly we saw in seed variance for FP8. Slide 18 shows seed runs where outputs differ in 8% of cases; we traced to microkernels and batch ordering.
[08:45] Priya: any short term mitigation?
[08:47] Sam: we can lock kernel ordering and set determinism mode — cost a bit in perf — or we can use FP8 for non-deterministic routes only.
[08:57] Priya: we need determinism for logging and reproducibility, so maybe lock kernel ordering for safety routes.
[09:03] Alex: agreed. We'll propose a hybrid: deterministic FP16 for safety prompts, high-throughput FP8/INT8 for analytics routes.
[09:12] Mark: how about cost modelling? can you walk quick through the cost delta sheet?
[09:17] Alex: sure — in chat the tab 'cost-delta' shows per-token cost after infra discounts. Key numbers: FP16 baseline $0.0018/token equivalent; INT8 approx $0.0009/token; FP8 approx $0.0008/token. Those are illustrative for our env.
[09:36] Priya: so roughly 50% savings with INT8. If safety prompts are 12% of volume and run FP16, net saving ~44% overall.
[09:45] Alex: yep that's correct with our model. We'll attach the sheet.
[09:49] (00:09:49) Priya: any other blockers we haven't covered?
[09:52] Elena: I'd like a short security memo: KMS integration, audit logs, where keys live, rotation, RBAC for rollback triggers.
[09:59] Alex: will do. I'll add a one-pager to the POC docs.
[10:04] Sam: final technical ask: we want to test prefix-cache-in-FP16 while model is INT8. That reduces cache quantization noise. If you can provide example long-context prompts we can run that config.
[10:18] Priya: will add 200 long-context examples to the folder.
[10:21] Sam: perfect.
[10:23] (00:10:23) Priya: timeline recap? when do you think we can have the 50k run results?
[10:27] Sam: if Redwood runs it on our infra, we can deliver by 2026-03-23; if you run it, depends on your infra but we'd help.
[10:34] Priya: Redwood run fine, security ok with infra?
[10:36] Elena: we'll need SOC2 doc and data handling note first.
[10:40] Alex: I'll send those now — link in chat.
[10:44] (00:10:44) Mark: small note — when you ran the FP8 seed sweep, did you fix RNG seeds? we saw some variance.
[10:50] Sam: seeds fixed for per-seed reproduction but kernel nondeterminism still caused mismatch. We'll lock kernel ordering as part of the next run.
[10:59] Priya: great.
[11:01] (00:11:01) Sam: okay wrapping up — action items as in chat: 50k run, prompt family list, security pack, cost delta. Anything else?
[11:09] Priya: please include a short A/B test plan for gradual rollout in the docs; we need to approve before canary.
[11:15] Alex: will include.
[11:17] Elena: also include the audit log retention period options.
[11:20] Alex: noted.
[11:22] (00:11:22) Priya: thanks everyone.
[11:24] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with the 50k plan and cost sheet today.
[11:28] (00:11:28) [END]
